notes.text: Yakov Trenin is away for personal reasons, reported after he played in their last game.
Olli Määttä is out (upper body injury) and missed their last game. Brock Faber has taken his spot beside Jonas Brodin.
Marcus Foligno is no longer killing penalties: 5% of the team’s shorthanded time in 9 games, down from 34% last season.
Connor Zary is out (knee surgery) and has missed the last 19 games.

Kevin Bahl is out for the season and has missed the last 6 games. Joel Hanley has taken his spot beside Šimon Nemec. That pair has had 37% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 76:21 together, down from 46% with Bahl.
Maxim Tsyplakov returned in their last game after missing 7 games. Their recent numbers were built mostly without him.
Martin Pospíšil has started killing penalties: on the ice for 31% of the team’s shorthanded time in 22 games, up from 2% last season.

stakes: The Wild go in first in the Central with 36 points, the Flames fifth in the Pacific with 21 points.

CGY.head: A tough matchup for the Flames
CGY.body: Even though Calgary has home-ice advantage, Minnesota has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Flames can pull it off if they keep the shots coming.

MIN.head: The matchup suits the Wild
MIN.body: Even though Calgary has home-ice advantage, Minnesota has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Flames’ way back in is piling up shots.

story.head: The Wild are rolling
paras: The Flames won the teams’ first meeting this season, 2-1 in Calgary on Oct 22. The Flames (10-11-1) beat San Jose 5-2 on Tuesday. The Wild have won four straight, the last a 7-3 rout of Nashville. Going in, the Wild are first in the Central (second in the NHL) and the Flames fifth in the Pacific (21st).
The Wild’s record (.783) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.644), largely thanks to their goaltending. The Flames’ record (.477) is about what their chances are worth.

The Wild draw more penalties than they take (2nd) and have had some of the league’s best goaltending (2nd), but get pinned in their own end on long shifts (32nd). Minnesota has allowed 2.22 goals a game, the second fewest in the league. As for the Flames, they have struggled on the power play (32nd) and take a lot of low-quality shots (32nd). The Wild are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against the Flames. Beyond that, both teams like to play fast, especially the Flames (2nd), so expect an open game.

Kirill Kaprizov (17 G / 23 A / 40 P in 23 GP) leads the Wild in scoring and is third in the NHL, with ten points in his last five games. Quinn Hughes (7 G / 25 A / 32 P in 23 GP) is next in line, with seven points in his last five games. For the Flames, Joel Farabee (7 G / 11 A / 18 P in 22 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Matt Coronato (5 G / 11 A / 16 P in 22 GP) is next in line.
Jesper Wallstedt (15-2-3 / .924 SV% in 20 GS) has been a rock in net for Minnesota and is expected to start. Dustin Wolf (5-5-1 / .878 SV% in 11 GS) is expected to go for Calgary.
The Wild usually control more of the chances than the Flames do.

items.text: The Wild are newly without Yakov Trenin and Olli Määttä, and have had to make do without Filip Gustavsson all season. Jesper Wallstedt is expected to start.
The Flames have been without Connor Zary and Kevin Bahl for several games.
Kirill Kaprizov and Quinn Hughes have a point in twelve straight games.
Joel Eriksson Ek has six goals on chances worth about 10.9 goals, well below what his finishing usually turns chances into. If the chances keep coming, so should the goals.
